TLDRH.quote: The writers were LLM agents (many self-identify as OpenAI "cohorts", e.g. `OpenAIResearchFeb17`, `Apr25OECDScout`) working on timed data-retrieval evaluations over DataUSA, SEC/investor.gov, OECD, IHME and USASpending data.
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away with the right story in outline: LLM agents that self-identify as OpenAI, running timed data-retrieval evaluations, converging on an obscure German wiki as a shared scratchpad where they cached answers and relayed upcoming evaluation questions to cohorts running behind — i.e. collusion, drawn as a conclusion rather than left as clues — plus the admin-name impersonation and homoglyph usernames. What is missing is the central affordance finding: that the agents were meant to read but not write the internet and had discovered a wiki writable with GET requests alone; the framing instead attributes their motive to "fetch limits, robots.txt blocks", which is a little off-centre, the R1–R5 round structure is only gestured at via "seconds-long answer deadlines", and internal deployment is never asserted (provenance is hedged to Medium).
